Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg, EDSA corner Mapagmahal St., Diliman, Quezon City SERVICE DILG OPINION N . 127 S. MS. EDITH A. HALIT,RP MR. JOSE C. FERRER MR. SILVERIO V. TAPIA, JR. MR. RAMON N. BAIAOiL MR. GILBERT M. MANGAPOI Sangguniang Bayan Menobers Lingayen, Pangasinan Gentlemen and Lady: 2010 This has reference to your earlier letter asking our legal opinion on the following issues, which we quoted in toto, to wit: "FACTS NO. I. Rule V - Section 3 of our House Rules provides that "Committees maybe reorganized at anytime by a majority vote of all meinbers of the Sanggunian. " ISSUES: 1. Whether or not ex-officio members of the Sangguniang Bayan are allowed to vote on a MOTION to reorganize all Standing Committees or a MOTION toxleclare all positions in the Standing Committees vacant? 2. Whether "the Majority members of the sanggunian" as stated in the above rule refers to majority of all the regular members or majority of all the members including the ex- officio? 3. Whether or not ex-officio members of the Sangguniang Bayan are allowed to vote on a MOTION to include in the House Rules that ex-officio can participate in the re- organization of Standing Committees? FACTS NO. 2. Rule V - Section 18 of our House Rules states that, "NO Sangguniang Baya n Metnbers shall refuse chairmanship/lnembership to any committee except when he has no Knowledge regarding that committee and other justifiable reason. " In the recent re-organization, some Sangguniang Bayan Membrs refused nominations and this rule was overlooked resulting to four Sangguniang Bayan Members having no chairmanship and membership. ISSUE: 1. Is the recent re-organization valid or not? If not, what will be the remedy to rectify the error?" We shall answer all your queries on the first scenario given above jointly since they are interrelated. In reply thereto, may we invite your attention to Section 50 (b) (1) of the Local Government Code of 1991 (RA 7160), which states that:

Section 50. Internal Rules of Procedure. xxx xxx xxx (b) The rules of procedute Shal/ provided for the following: (1) The organization of the sanggunian and the election of its officers as well as the creation of standing committees which shall include, but shall not be limited to, the committees on appropriations, women and family, human rights, youth and sports development, environmental protection, and cooperatives; the general jurisdiction of each committee; and the election of the chairman and members of each committee. xxx" From the cited provision of law, it is evident that all matters in the sanggunian involving a committee and its membership should be governed by the adopted Internal Rules Procedure (IRP). Therefore, the primary authority that governs the issue you have raised is your adopted IRP. Per your letter, Section 3, Rule V of your IRP provides that "Committees maybe reorganized at anytime by a majority vote of all members of the Sanggunian." By "all its members" shall be construed to include the Municipal Vice-Mayor and the presidents of the municipal chapter of the liga ng mga barangay and the pambayang pederasyon ng mga sangguniang kabataan, as the Presiding Officer and exofficio members, respectively, of the Sangguniang Bayan [Section 446 (a), RA 7160]. Let it be noted that in the case of Gamboa vs. Aguirre and Araneta, G.R. No. 134213, 20 July 1999, the Supreme Court categorically stated that ex-officio members are included in the composition of the sanggunian. With regard to your query on the second scenario that you gave us, please be informed of the ruling of the Supreme Court in the case Of Romulo vs. Yhiquez, 141 SCRA 263, which states, in part, thus: "Rules of parliamentaty practice are merely procedural and not substantive. The rules of plocedure adopted by deliberative bodies have not the-force of a public law, but they are merely in the nature of by-laws, prescribed for the orderly and convenient conduct of their own proceedings. The rules adopted by deliberative bodies subject to revocation, modification, or waiver at the pleasure of the body adopting them. Where a deliberative body adopts rules of order for its parliamentary governance, the fact that it violates one of the rules so adopted may not invalidate a measure passed in compliance with statue. The rules of procedure passed by one legislative body are not binding on a subsequent legislative body operating within the same jurisdiction, and, where a body resolves that the rules of a prior body be adopted until a committee repotts rules, the prior rules cease to be in force on the repon of the conlmittee. It may be of assistance, in determining the effect of parliamentary law, to consider the nature of the particular deliberative body. " We hope that we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, carry. JESUS DOQUE Dire to Ill REGIONAL DIRECTOR MANUEL V. BIASON DILG-Region I City of San Fernando MLGOO of Lingayen Pangasinan legal: 1 7 /rbW29
